name: Harribance: Koren helmet, 4 coil pairs x 0.5 s, five conditions (Persinger 2010)
origin: Persinger & Koren lab (Laurentian University), Koren Helmet session with the psychic Sean Harribance, reported in Persinger 2010
summary: The Koren-helmet session Persinger's lab ran with the psychic Sean Harribance: no field, 3.3 Hz and 1.6 Hz sine waves, burst-firing and an LTP (primed-burst) pattern, 2-3 min each, stepped around four left-right coil pairs every 0.5 s with the right side about 10% stronger. Persinger reported 22 presence or vision button presses during the LTP pattern against 5-12 for the others, with a 6:1 left-side bias (one subject).
notes: Persinger 2010 describes the Koren Helmet as four pairs of solenoids "arranged in an elliptical pattern at the level of temporoparietal region", fed by a commutator that sends the pattern to each of the four pairs in turn for 0.5 s (2 s per full rotation); Persinger & Murphy 2016 add that one solenoid on the left and one on the right are on at any moment. The fields were "weak (1 uT)". Here each side carries four coils on a small ellipse over the temporoparietal region (T7, C5, CP5, TP7 and T8, C6, CP6, TP8), stepped in mirror image; the exact positions and stepping order are not published. The right side was set about 10% stronger (about 100 nT per 10 cm), so the left coils run at 0.91. In a 45-min setting Harribance received no field, 3.3 Hz, 1.6 Hz, burst-firing and LTP in counterbalanced order for 2-3 min each; how often each came and in which order is not given, so this runs two passes of 3 min each (30 min), the second in roughly reverse order. The sines' point duration is not given (1 ms here). Burst-firing is the lab's analgesic pattern presented once every 4 s (Martin et al. 2004); its point values are unpublished, so the built-in accelerating burst of 230 points at 3 ms (0.69 s) stands in. LTP is described as "a single pulse followed about 170 msec later by 4 pulses in rapid succession with a functional frequency of between 100 and 200 Hz"; it is built as 1-ms positive pulses at 0, 170, 175, 180 and 185 ms, repeating every 200 ms. The repetition rate is not given; 5 per second follows the lab's "1 s pulse of 5 trains" LTP field (Delparte & Persinger 2007). The 200-Hz spacing (the top of the stated range, which keeps the next primer 15 ms clear of the burst), the polarity, the 1-ms points and the repetition rate are assumptions; the project's primed generator instead uses the 150-ms primer interval of a later Shiva LTP file (Corradini 2014) with 100-Hz pulses. The left:right ratio of presses was 1.5-2.1:1 for the other conditions and 6:1 for LTP; Roll et al. 2002 likewise reported left-sided presences with LTP-patterned fields over his right temporoparietal region. The "Harribance configuration" of Persinger & Saroka 2012 is his own digitised EEG, not part of this program, and cannot be rebuilt without the original data. One subject, unblinded, button counts only, reported years later in a NeuroQuantology paper. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on headache, nausea or distress.
setting: Seated and blindfolded in a quiet, dark room, holding a button or tally counter in each hand: press the left or right one when you sense a presence or see a vision on that side, both when it is in front of or behind you. Have someone else note which condition was running, or use the app's Blind option.
schedule: One session in the original (one subject).
source: Persinger 2010, The Harribance effect as pervasive out-of-body experiences, NeuroQuantology 8(4):444-465, pp. 448-449 and 454 http://web.archive.org/web/20150426091303id_/http://www.neuroquantology.com/index.php/journal/article/download/301/346 ; Persinger & Murphy 2016, Neuroscience & Medicine 7:27-44 (Koren Helmet: four left-right solenoid pairs, 0.5 s each, 2-s cycle) https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/god-helmet/god_helmet_debate_publication.htm ; Roll, Persinger, Webster, Tiller & Cook 2002, Int J Neurosci 112:197-224 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12325407/ ; Persinger & Saroka 2012, Protracted parahippocampal activity associated with Sean Harribance, Int J Yoga 5:140-145 https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3410194/ ; Martin & Persinger 2004, Neurosci Lett 366:226-229 (burst-firing once every 4 s) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15276252/ ; Persinger, Hoang & Baker-Price 2009 (burst-firing about 0.7 s once every 3 s) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20017628/ ; Delparte & Persinger 2007, Int J Neurosci 117:295-299 (LTP field as "1 s pulse of 5 trains") https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17365115/ ; Corradini 2014, MA thesis, Laurentian University (primed-burst LTP file) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/1455e1f3-2f1d-47b5-93cd-23713d69e651 ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1-6 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
